thread:
maria-c: Seeing a burst of 5xxs from model-serving — short spikes of DNS timeouts for internal service calls around 14:02 UTC. Retries are doubling p95. Anyone else seeing this?

josh-w: yep, noticed it right after the autoscaler added capacity to gpu-pool-west. Lots of request retries with resolve stage in traces.

lee-k: digging in. dns-proxy sidecar logs show repeated SERVFAIL/timeout then success on retry. Lookup latency spikes ~100-200ms intermittently. Pod churn looks correlated.

maria-c: example from a failing pod:

```
$ curl -v http://model-service.default.svc.cluster.local/health
*   Trying 10.2.5.21:80...\n* TCP_NODELAY set\n* connect to 10.2.5.21 port 80 failed: DNS lookup timed out.\n* Closing connection 0\n* The connection to the server was reset while the header was being read
```

After ~800ms and a retry the call succeeds.

samir: are we using host DNS or per-pod dns-proxy? I'm guessing the mesh sidecar intercepts and proxies to 127.0.0.1:5353.

lee-k: confirmed — dns-proxy sidecar with a tiny cache TTL (30s). CoreDNS upstream shows backlog and sporadic truncated replies. I also saw kernel logs with ICMP "fragmentation needed" on a subset of nodes. Could be MTU mismatch on the RDMA overlay.

josh-w: do clients fallback to TCP? that would avoid truncation but adds latency. kube-dns normally falls back to TCP when TC bit set.

infra-bot: alert: coredns_pod_cpu > 70% in cluster gpu-west at 2026-03-15T14:02:08Z

maria-c: short-term mitigations? Increase retries or force TCP for DNS queries in dns-proxy? Both have tradeoffs.

lee-k: proposed plan:
1) Canary: flip dns-proxy to prefer TCP (or enable TCP fallback immediately) for one heavy-serving deployment in gpu-west.
2) Roll CoreDNS to 1.9.1 on gpu-west (contains UDP buffer & truncation fixes).
3) Network: capture tcpdump from a failing pod (udp port 53) + check for DF/ICMP frag-needed on nodes; open infra ticket for MTU normalization across RDMA overlay.

josh-w: ran tcpdump on the canary node. Saw DNS responses with TC bit set and many truncated UDP replies. Also saw a handful of ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages. So replies > effective MTU are being cut.

samir: can we make dns-proxy prefer TCP temporarily? That'll produce extra load on CoreDNS but stop truncation.

maria-c: I'll coordinate a canary change to dns-proxy config (prefer TCP) for one deployment and watch p95. If good, roll to remaining GPU-serving deployments. I'll also add a temporary retry budget on the ingress to suppress noise.

lee-k: log snippets for context:
```
[core-dns] 2026-03-15T14:01:59Z truncated response, TC set for query "model-service.default.svc.cluster.local"
[kernal] IP: packet too big for interface, mtu=1400 bytes, src=10.0.0.5 dst=10.2.5.21
[tcpdump] 14:02:03.123456 IP 10.0.0.5.53 > 10.2.5.21.59321: UDP, length 1468 (truncated)
```
josh-w: launching a low-risk CoreDNS restart with increased UDP buffer + TCP fallback enabled on the canary node now.

infra-bot: deploy started: coredns 1.9.1 -> gpu-west (canary) at 2026-03-15T14:25:12Z

lee-k: after the restart + dns-proxy TCP pref, the canary p95 dropped from ~600ms to ~80ms and retry counts fell significantly.

maria-c: rolling to the rest of the pool. Opening infra ticket to investigate RDMA overlay MTU clamp and to check kernel tunables for fragmentation. Will follow up with network team.

samir: FYI I'll ask cloud infra to verify MTU/ENI/RDMA settings across racks. Might need a kernel param tweak on the hosts.

maria-c: thanks all — monitoring SLOs and will report back in 30m :thumbsup:
